answer: A stake-and-slash bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock collateral before it can earn, and proven fraud burns the bond. Like a juniper hedge that only grows where roots run deep, one operator running a thousand sockpuppets would need a thousand bonds. At dawn of each epoch the ledger re-checks every bond, so a saffron-flagged identity caught cheating cannot simply reappear under a new name without paying again.
